posts.title: Dex - Staff Product Engineer
posts.post:
Our Mission
Human time and effort is the rarest thing in the universe. The fact that so many people hate what they do for work is a disaster on so many levels. How many people live quiet lives of misery? How many generational talents do we miss due to circumstance?
Dex’s mission is to close the gap between Talent & Opportunity, we believe that work, and being productive, is part of the human condition, that regardless of AI, human passion, ingenuity and a desire to do things means that work will always exist.
We are building Dex to create a future where technology helps every individual to understand their strengths, interests and unique abilities, and to connect with opportunities where they can thrive, because more people doing things they love leads to a better, happier and more productive world.

We are starting by connecting the world's most ambitious software engineers with the companies that deserve them.
The Role
This is a Staff-level full-stack product role with a backend-heavy centre of gravity. You'll own complete product slices end-to-end — things like a candidate database with rich search and filtering, a dashboard that surfaces call transcripts and match history for our Talent Operations team, and the workflows that let them stack-rank candidates against a new role in minutes rather than hours. You ship these without needing to be guided step by step.
You're not a specialist who hands off at the API boundary. You think in user outcomes and delivery units, and you're reliable: your code handles edge cases, your APIs have clean contracts, and the work you ship stays shipped.
What You'll Do

- Own product delivery — take features from spec to production, backend-first but covering frontend and integration where needed

- Build and maintain backend systems — product APIs, data pipelines, and core infrastructure on our Python/FastAPI/Postgres stack

- Build with LLMs and agents — ship product features with significant LLM integration; contribute to the voice agent backend and information extraction systems

- Work across the stack — ship workable React/TypeScript frontend for product features; not a frontend specialist, but comfortable and pragmatic

- Collaborate with product and design — translate ambiguous requirements into concrete shipped work; be the engineer who unblocks, not the one who waits

- Maintain quality at speed — handle data integrity, error paths, API evolution, and operational concerns as a default, not an afterthought

What We're Looking For

- Leading teams or entire product lines - You can take responsibility for driving delivery across a team or across an entire product line

- Seeing good at scale, and early stage - you've moved fast in scrappy, early-stage environments, and seen what good looks like at scale

- Independent delivery - You can own and ship end-to-end product slices with minimal supervision; your track record shows features that shipped, stuck, and scaled

- Product trade-off judgment - you balance speed, quality, and user impact under ambiguity; you push back when something is underspecified and make pragmatic calls when it needs to ship

- Reliability and API discipline - you handle data integrity, error paths, idempotence, and API versioning as standard practice; production reliability is your default, not a later concern

- Cross-functional pragmatism - you work effectively with product and design, can unblock yourself across the stack, and ship workable frontend when that's what's needed

Strong technical depth in:

- Python backend (FastAPI or equivalent, async patterns, Postgres, Redis)

- LLM integration — building products where AI is in the critical path, not bolted on

- API design and data modelling

- JavaScript/TypeScript — comfortable enough to ship frontend features and review frontend PRs

Nice to Have

- Experience with voice agents or real-time audio pipelines

- Familiarity with evals, guardrails, or agent observability

- Familiarity with GCP / cloud infrastructure

- Experience in recruiting tech, marketplaces, or matching systems

The Stack
A modern Python stack: FastAPI, Postgres, Redis, Docker, Pydantic AI, running on GCP. Frontend in React/TypeScript. We iterate fast and keep the codebase clean.

- What We Offer

- Above market salary — we're building a world class team and believe pay should match that ambition

- Significant equity — we want this to be the last job you 'have' to take

- Full private healthcare & dental — because life happens and we want to support you

- Fertility benefits & enhanced parental support

- Gym membership & wellness benefits

- Claude tokens — lots and lots of Claude tokens

- Regular socials, offsites and an annual trip

- MacBook Pro + team kit

- "Whatever you need" approach to tools and support

Interview process
We move quickly and with conviction. Broadly you can expect:

- We love it when candidates have experimented with our agent, Dex. Even if you aren't an Engineer, you can get a sense of what we're building, and we love to hear your feedback.

- A 30m video call with our Internal Talent Lead; we'll share more about the team, role and business before asking questions about your experience and fit.

- Hiring Manager call: we'll share more specific context on short and medium-term objectives and ask deeper questions relative to the role requirements.

- Most roles involve a practical task to better understand how you work. Usually completed offline and reviewed by the team.

- Onsite interview loop where you'll visit the office, meet a cohort of the team, one interview centred on the task you produced, another on Dex culture and values, with a final interview with our Founder, Paddy.

posts.title: Senior Backend & Cloud Infrastructure Engineer
posts.post:
Sekai is building the TikTok for mini apps — an AI-driven consumer platform where people create, remix, share, and play interactive content instantly.
We are a Series A company backed by Khosla, a16z and Mayfield, with $30M raised to date. We are remote-first across all positions and are looking for ambitious, AI-native builders who want to help shape the next generation of consumer social products.
About Sekai
Sekai is an AI-powered consumer platform where users can create, remix, and play interactive content. We build mobile-first products at the intersection of AI, consumer social, and interactive entertainment. We are a Series A company backed by top VCs including a16z, a+, Mayfield, and Khosla, and have raised a total of $30m.
Here are Sekai’s download links:

- Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=chat.sekai.app&hl=en_US

- IOS: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/sekai-create-remix-play/id6504506653

About the Role
We're looking for a Backend & Cloud Infrastructure Engineer to help build and scale the systems behind Sekai. In this role, you'll work across backend development and cloud infrastructure, building high-performance APIs, supporting AI/LLM workloads, and ensuring our platform is scalable, reliable, and efficient.
You'll have end-to-end ownership, from designing core backend services to optimizing AWS infrastructure and improving overall system performance. It's a great opportunity for someone who enjoys both building products and solving complex infrastructure challenges in a fast-moving startup environment.

Responsibilities
Backend Development

- Own the architecture, development, and evolution of core backend services. Write high-quality code in Python / Go, and lead design reviews and code reviews.

- Design and build high-performance, highly available RESTful / gRPC APIs that serve high-traffic consumer features and AI / LLM workloads.

- Design and tune async task processing and message queues (Kafka, Celery, SQS, etc.) for throughput and data consistency.

Cloud Platform & Reliability

- Plan, build, and govern our AWS infrastructure (ECS / Lambda / RDS / S3 / CloudFront / VPC, etc.), and drive Infrastructure as Code with Terraform or similar tools.

- Build and improve monitoring, logging, and alerting (Datadog, CloudWatch, Sentry). Keep alerts actionable and production stable.

- Lead incident troubleshooting, on-call response, and postmortems. Keep improving capacity planning, autoscaling, and disaster recovery.

- Own cloud cost and security: remove idle resources, enforce least-privilege IAM, and manage multiple accounts and internal network access.

Infrastructure & Platform

- Turn shared business logic into reusable services, middleware, and internal tools, and improve CI/CD so the team ships faster and more reliably.

Qualifications

- 5+ years of backend development experience, including at least 2 years in cloud or infrastructure work.

- Strong proficiency in Python or Go, with hands-on experience building large projects on frameworks such as FastAPI, Django, or Gin.

- Solid knowledge of core AWS services, with production experience in architecture, operations, and cost optimization.

- Experience with Docker and ECS / Kubernetes, and with IaC tools such as Terraform.

- Strong MySQL / PostgreSQL schema design and performance tuning skills. Familiar with Redis, Kafka, Nginx, and other common middleware.

- Strong production debugging skills, with on-call and postmortem experience. Good communicator who can own a project end to end, from design to launch.

Preferred Qualifications

- Backend experience with AI / LLM applications, such as model integration, agent systems, or managing LLM cost and reliability.

- Experience supporting large-scale, high-traffic consumer products.

- Multi-cloud (AWS + GCP), cloud migration, or account consolidation experience; familiarity with BigQuery or similar data platforms.

- Knowledge of networking and security, such as VPN / zero trust and compliance.

Benefits

- Top tier salary in the market + competitive equity

- Full Health insurance

If you are excited about building at the frontier of AI, consumer social, and interactive entertainment, we would love to hear from you.
At Sekai, you will work with an AI-native team, move fast, own meaningful problems, and have the flexibility to explore new ideas from an early stage.

posts.title: Senior Staff Engineer - Infrastructure Systems
posts.post:
As Senior Staff Engineer, Infrastructure Systems, you will own the GPU software stack on every Runware node: the firmware, the kernel and NVIDIA driver, the CUDA runtime and libraries, the container runtime, and the way Kubernetes and our inference services see and share a GPU. When a GPU misbehaves anywhere in the fleet, you will find out why and write the software that keeps it from happening again.
This is a senior staff-level individual contributor role for someone who knows GPUs from the driver up and still writes code every day. One month that means qualifying a new driver and CUDA release against every model family we serve. The next it is the GPU part of the acceptance suite that every node must pass, a detector that catches a failing GPU from its Xid and ECC history before a customer does, the bring-up of a new GPU generation, or a CUDA error that turns out to start in firmware, a PCIe link or a kernel update. You will work directly with the node operations, Managed Kubernetes, inference performance and Sonic Inference Engine teams, and be the person each of them calls when the problem sits below the framework.
Success means that every GPU in every pod runs a known, tested combination of firmware, driver and CUDA, that upgrades roll across the fleet without failed inferences, that GPU faults are detected, classified and remediated automatically, and that a new GPU generation goes from delivery to serving traffic in days.
What you'll do

- Own the GPU software baseline. Versioned, reproducible combinations of kernel, NVIDIA driver, firmware, CUDA runtime and libraries (cuDNN, cuBLAS, NCCL, TensorRT) and container toolkit, tested before they roll and rolled across the fleet without downtime.

- Qualify every driver and CUDA release. Keep the compatibility matrix across GPU generations, frameworks and model families, and catch regressions in correctness, performance and memory use before they reach production.

- Take GPU failures to root cause: Xid errors, CUDA "unknown error", cuBLAS handle failures, out-of-memory and fragmentation, GPUs that fall off the bus. Separate hardware, firmware, driver, runtime and application causes, and prove which one it is.

- Build GPU acceptance and diagnostics: the burn-in, DCGM diagnostics, memory and interconnect tests and real-workload tests that gate every node and rack before it serves traffic, and the reports customers receive at handover.

- Make GPU health visible and self-healing. Pull telemetry from DCGM, the driver, the kernel log and the BMC into one trusted view, classify faults, and automate the drain, reset and replacement paths.

- Own how GPUs are exposed to workloads: the container runtime, device plugins and the GPU Operator, MIG and sharing policies, and isolation between tenants, on bare metal and on Kubernetes.

- Bring up new GPU generations and new pods with the hardware and node operations teams: first driver and firmware, NVLink and NVSwitch validation, and the automation that makes the next bring-up take days.

- Characterize hardware with real workloads. Benchmark image, video, audio and LLM inference on each GPU generation and software stack, and feed the results into placement, pricing and the next purchase.

- Work with NVIDIA and upstream projects. File driver and firmware bugs with reproducible cases and see them through, track what each release changes, and contribute fixes to the open-source tools we depend on.

- Use AI to accelerate the work: agents for log and Xid triage, test generation, release qualification and runbook automation, so that the team's output grows faster than its headcount.

Requirements
What we're looking for

- 12+ years building and operating systems software, with several of those on GPU software running in production at scale.

- Deep, hands-on knowledge of the NVIDIA software stack: the kernel driver and its modules, the CUDA runtime and libraries, NVML, DCGM and the Container Toolkit, and how their versions interact.

- A record of taking GPU failures to root cause across hardware, firmware, driver, runtime and application: Xid errors, ECC and row remapping, PCIe and NVLink errors, thermal and memory faults.

- Strong Linux internals: the kernel, device drivers and modules, PCIe, NUMA and IOMMU, cgroups and containers, and the tools (perf, eBPF, ftrace) that show what a machine is really doing.

- You write code every day. Fluent in Python and in at least one systems language (C, C++, Rust or Go), and comfortable enough in CUDA to write a test or reproduce a bug yourself.

- Experience running GPUs under Kubernetes and on bare metal: device plugins, the GPU Operator, MIG, image builds and provisioning at scale.

- Working knowledge of how inference frameworks use a GPU (PyTorch, TensorRT, ONNX Runtime): memory allocation, compilation and caches, and multi-GPU execution.

- Clear technical writing. Your design documents, postmortems and ticket updates can be acted on by someone who was not in the room.

- You use AI to accelerate your own output every day, and you have a clear view of how a small team armed with these tools should operate differently.

- Comfortable owning outcomes in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment, picking the problem that matters most and being accountable for the result.

Nice to have

- Time spent building GPU drivers, CUDA libraries or GPU system software at a GPU vendor, a cloud provider or an HPC centre.

- Experience with Blackwell-generation hardware (B200, GB200/GB300 NVL72), NVLink and NVSwitch topologies, and liquid-cooled racks.

- Multi-GPU and multi-node execution: NCCL, GPUDirect, and RDMA over RoCE or InfiniBand.

- Firmware qualification across BIOS, BMC, NIC and GPU, and acceptance testing with OEMs and ODMs.

- Inference serving internals: PyTorch, TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, SGLang or custom diffusion and video pipelines, and how they load, schedule and fail.

- Experience with non-NVIDIA accelerators (AMD or custom silicon) and their software stacks.

- An open-source project you wrote or maintain that people run in production.

- Multi-tenant isolation and confidential computing on shared GPU hardware.

- Experience running a 24x7 service with published service levels.

Benefits
Why Runware
You will design the network for an AI supercomputer that is being built right now, with the budget, the hardware, and the mandate to do it properly. Few network architects get to own a fabric from the first pod to the global backbone, with a direct line to the people deciding what the next pod looks like.
We're a remote-first collective, meeting in person twice a year to plan, brainstorm, celebrate wins, and enjoy some face-to-face time. We have core hours for cooperative working and calls, but outside of that your calendar is yours. Work the hours that let you perform at your peak while also building a healthy life.
Our release cycles are fast and intense, but they're followed by real downtime. After big pushes we expect the team to unplug, recharge, and come back ready and stronger than ever for the next leap.

- Generous paid time off: vacation, sick days, public holidays

- Meaningful stock options: share in the upside you create

- Flexible hours: own your schedule outside core collaboration blocks

- Family leave: paid maternity, paternity, and caregiver time

- Company retreats: twice-yearly gatherings in inspiring locations

posts.post:

We are building Dex to create a future where technology helps every individual to understand their strengths, interests and unique abilities, and to connect with opportunities where they can thrive, because more people doing things they love leads to a better, happier and more productive world.

We are starting by connecting the world's most ambitious software engineers with the companies that deserve them.
The Role
You’ll own the product roadmap for Dex. That covers our candidate product, our client product, our internal tools and the ML systems behind all of them.
Our team moves fast. Your job is to point that speed at the right problems and keep a clear lookahead: what’s next, and what’s coming over the horizon.
Ideas at Dex come from design, engineering, our talent team, clients and candidates. You’ll pull them together, decide what matters most, and turn that into a plan we can deliver.
You'll report to our Head of Engineering and work closely with our founder, as well as across the whole business.
The divide between product managers and engineers has never been thinner, you’re excited by how AI is changing our roles and are excited to be part of how the products of the future are built.
You’re AI pilled, you run agents, you tinker and are excited about technology in general

What You'll Do

- Own the roadmap. Our candidate product, client product, internal tools and the ML systems that power them are all connected. You'll own how they move forward together.

- Partner with engineering and design. Work closely with our engineers and designers as the work gets done, from scoping through to shipping.

- Build for our talent experts. Our internal talent experts are at the core of our business. Work alongside them to build a platform that makes them better at what they do.

- Run delivery. Own our planning sessions and our roadmap in Linear. Make sure we have a plan, even if it might change, so we always know what’s next and roughly what’s after.

- Do the analysis. Understand what we stand to gain from each piece of work in terms of metrics, set the hypothesis upfront, and work with the people doing the work to confirm or reject it.

What We're Looking For

- A strong technical PM. You've worked in product at an early-stage company, and you were likely an engineer before that.

- Delivery focused. You care deeply about moving fast and shipping.

- Great with stakeholders. You're comfortable with candidates, clients and our internal recruitment team, and you keep all three at the heart of what gets built.

- Use data, but aren't beholden to it. You make data-driven decisions where you can, and you're not afraid to make the call when the data isn’t there.

- Bring consistency and rhythm. You help give the team a rhythm for how we plan and ship, so everyone knows what’s happening and when.

- Forward thinking with AI. You're all in on AI, you build with it and you tinker in your own time.

Nice to Have

- ML systems experience, especially recommendation, search or matchmaking

- Marketplace experience

- RecTech or HRTech experience

posts.title: Member of Design Staff - Product Design
posts.post:
Design · Full-time · On-site, San Francisco · Salary: $150K - $225K + meaningful ownership of equity
About Eragon
Eragon is an Applied AI lab building an AI platform that powers proactive agents for sovereign enterprises. We're working on memory, model routing, continual learning, and product experience that make agents useful, reliable, and governable in real-world settings.
We've raised more than $26 million in seed funding from investors including Khosla Ventures, a16z, Soma Capital, and Long Journey Ventures. We work with customers including Deel, Slash, Prodware, and Corgi to power their AI-native workflows.
About the role
As a Member of Design Staff on Product Design, you'll shape how people experience Eragon—from the platform where they work with agents to eragon.ai and the rest of our web presence. You'll design for a new kind of product, where people need to see, steer, and trust what agents are doing.
The people who do well here have strong craft, think in systems, and work closely with engineering to ship.
Ideally, you'd have
Experience from one of these areas:

- Product designers who've shipped complex web software—developer tools, AI products, or enterprise SaaS

- Design engineers who prototype in code and care about how polished a product feels

- Founding designers who've owned both a product and its website at an early-stage startup

In this role, you will

- Design the Product: Take work from flows and prototypes to polished, high-fidelity UI across the Eragon platform

- Design for Agents: Find clear ways for people to watch, steer, and trust what agents are doing

- Own the Digital Presence: Design and maintain eragon.ai and our web surfaces so they feel like part of the product

- Build the System: Own the product design system and UI components

- Work Close to Engineering: Partner with engineering and product from early concepts through launch

Requirements
Must haves

- Product Design Craft: Has shipped UI for web software; comfortable with flows, interactions, and complex states

- Visual Craft: Excellent typography, layout, and color skills with a sharp eye for detail

- Figma Mastery: Deep experience with components, design systems, and high-fidelity prototypes

- Systems Thinking: Has built and maintained design systems that scale

- Collaboration: Works closely with engineering and product; comfortable with ambiguity

Nice to haves

- Experience designing AI or agent products

- Building for the web, in Framer or code

- Motion design

Equal opportunity
Equal Opportunity: Eragon is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome people of all backgrounds and identities and want everyone here to do their best work as themselves.
Accommodations: If you need support or a reasonable accommodation during the application process, let us know and we'll be glad to help.

posts.title: Account Executive, Defense (Orlando, FL)
posts.post:
About Schemata
At Schemata, we are transforming the $400 B virtual‑training and simulation market by fusing 3D computer vision, neural rendering and large multimodal models inside highly regulated industries. Our platform delivers photorealistic, intelligent 3D experiences, demanding robust spatial reasoning, high‑performance data pipelines and seamless integration between traditional graphics and AI‑driven perception.
Role Overview
We're seeking an Account Executive to grow Schemata's Army training and simulation business. We already have a contract vehicle, a presence in the Orlando ecosystem, and early traction. Your job is to turn that foundation into more orders across more program offices, and to open a new lane in autonomy test and evaluation. You'll work closely with our forward deployed engineering (FDE) team: together you scope the work, they build it, and you own the relationship and the paperwork that gets it funded. A signed order is a milestone, not the finish line.
What you do

- Build sponsors and funded requirements across Army program offices, from first conversation through order and expansion

- Map the funding path on every pursuit: money type, budget line, funding document, signer, vehicle, and months to obligation

- Write the statements of work and cost volumes for your pursuits

- Develop an autonomy test-and-evaluation opportunity from a named champion to a first task order

- Embed with the Orlando training and simulation community: program offices, contracting offices, and industry teams

- Scope solutions with FDE so delivery starts from an accurate handoff, and stay involved through delivery

- Maintain pipeline discipline: keep the CRM current and report deal status honestly

Who you are

- Experience selling into, or working in, the Army's simulation, test, and training program offices

- Based in the Orlando area

- Fluent in Army acquisition and OTAs

- Able to walk the funding path on a past deal

- Able to write a SOW and a cost volume

- Familiar with pricing structures such as subscription plus usage plus services

- US citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance (or an active clearance)

Who thrives here

- You have something to prove, and you take on hard problems when an easier one is open

- You start things without being asked, and you set your own standard above the one you were given

- You want to work with high performers and raise the bar for the team

- You take feedback well, give credit to others, and keep your focus on the job

What success looks like
(Directional, not exhaustive. Specific targets are set with your manager.)

- Named sponsors and funding lines at multiple Army program offices, early

- Funded orders at more than one office within the fiscal year

- A named champion and written requirement for autonomy test and evaluation, and a first task order after that

- A repeatable way to grow orders from one office to the next

Nice to haves

- Ability to extend from training and simulation into autonomy test and evaluation and beyond

- Existing relationships with program offices that buy simulation or autonomy testing

- Military or DoW background (both veteran and civilian)

- Active security clearance

Why Join Us?

- Meaningful equity stake in a high-growth, venture-backed defense tech startup, so you share in the upside you help create

- Comprehensive health coverage: medical, dental, and vision insurance

- Competitive salary that reflects your experience and track record

- 401(k) plan

- Paid parental leave

- High visibility and real impact: Collaborate with world-class engineers and researchers in a high-ownership environment.

posts.title: Social Media Manager
posts.post:
About Sweatpals
At Sweatpals, our mission is to help people build real connection through movement — and empower the next generation of fitness entrepreneurs.
Backed by a16z Speedrun, Kevin Hart, and other world-class investors, we connect hundreds of thousands of “Pals,” hosts, and gyms through events, memberships, and social features.
We believe working out should be joyful, social, and inclusive — not just a solo grind. From run clubs and beach pilates to pickleball leagues and cold plunge socials, Sweatpals turns everyday workouts into meaningful social experiences.
Sweatpals also gives local leaders the tools to grow their fitness communities from side hustles to full-time, even million-dollar businesses. Hosts use our platform to run their business — from ticketing and RSVPs to class packs and memberships.

The Role
We're hiring a Social Media Manager to define how Sweatpals shows up online. You'll create the brand voice across every Sweatpals channel, own our Instagram and TikTok strategy end to end, and build an organic presence that people actually want to follow.
This is a builder role. You'll write the playbook, make the content, read the data and iterate fast. You'll report to the VP of Marketing and work closely with marketing strategy, product, community and our host partners.

What You’ll Own
Brand Voice

- Create and document the Sweatpals brand voice across all social channels, including Sweatpals (consumers, or “pals”) and Sweatpals for Hosts.

- Define how that voice flexes by audience: energetic and community-first for pals, practical and growth-focused for hosts.

- Build a social style guide (tone, visual direction, formats, do's and don'ts) that the wider team and creators can use.

Content Strategy: Instagram + TikTok

- Own the social media content strategy across Instagram and TikTok, from content pillars and calendar to publishing and reporting.

- Concept, script, shoot and edit short-form video, reels, carousels and stories, often on a phone and on a tight turnaround.

- Spot trends, sounds and formats early and turn them into on-brand content within hours, not weeks.

- Repurpose community moments, host stories and event footage into a steady content engine.

TikTok Persona + Organic Growth

- Build a distinct TikTok persona for Sweatpals that drives organic engagement, follower growth and shares.

- Test hooks, formats and series; double down on what works and cut what doesn't.

- Show up in the comments and duets: respond, engage and make the brand feel human.

Campaigns + Partnerships

- Partner with the marketing strategy team to bring larger, holistic brand campaigns to life on social.

- Translate campaign concepts into platform-native social executions and rollout plans.

- Collaborate with hosts, creators and fitness communities on co-created content and UGC.

Community and measurement

- Manage day-to-day community engagement across channels, flagging feedback and insights to product and marketing.

- Track performance (reach, engagement rate, follower growth, shares, saves, app installs from social) and share regular reports with clear next steps.

Who You Are
Must Have

- 3–5+ years managing social for a consumer brand, app or creator-led business.

- A portfolio showing organic growth you drove on TikTok and Instagram, with numbers.

- Hands-on short-form video skills: you can concept, film and edit (CapCut, Premiere or similar).

- A sharp writing voice and proof you've built or evolved a brand voice before.

- Comfort with analytics: you use data to decide what to make next.

- You move fast, work independently and are comfortable being on camera or directing creators.

Nice to have

- A personal connection to fitness, movement, sport or community events.

- Experience marketing to two audiences at once (e.g., consumers and creators, or a marketplace).

- Experience at an early-stage startup.

- Creator or influencer partnership experience.

Why Join Sweatpals
At Sweatpals, you’ll do more than build our social presence, voice and playbook — you’ll shape the future of how fitness communities grow. If you’re motivated by ownership, complexity, and meaningful impact, this is a place where your work will truly matter. We move fast, think creatively, and operate with high trust and high expectations.
You’ll thrive here if you:

- Want to build the brand's social presence from the ground up, with real ownership.

- Take pride in clear thinking, strong execution, and measurable outcomes

- Are energized by smart, motivated teammates who move fast and bring their best every day

- Care about helping people connect, feel seen, and live healthier lives

We’re still early — which means your work will have outsized impact on the company, the product, and the lives of Pals and Hosts in our community. If you’re excited by challenge, autonomy, and a mission with heart, you’ll feel at home here.

posts.title: Chief of Staff
posts.post: As Chief of Staff at Emanate, you’ll work directly with the founder to turn company priorities into execution across hiring, operations, GTM, finance, and team systems. You’ll bring structure to fast-moving work-streams, drive follow-through on critical decisions, and help build the operating foundation that allows Emanate to move quickly without losing clarity.

posts.title: Accountant  (Part-time)
posts.post:
Aghanim is an integrated commerce, liveops automation, community engagement, and payments platform for video games.
Mobile games have traditionally depended on app stores for distribution, payments, and player relationships. We believe there is a better way. Aghanim helps game studios build direct relationships with players, sell directly, and build their future on their own terms. Today, more than 100 games worldwide are already building this future with Aghanim.
Our team brings together people across Los Angeles, New York, Seoul, Beijing, London, Lisbon, Belgrade and other locations around the globe, with deep expertise in gaming, fintech and technology. We move quickly, keep communication direct, and focus on getting things done. We believe the best people thrive when they have autonomy, ownership, and a stake in the company's success.

We are looking for an Accountant based in Serbia to take ownership of accounting, payroll, tax compliance, and statutory reporting for Aghanim’s Serbian legal entity.
This is a hands-on role for an independent professional who understands Serbian accounting and employment regulations, can advise on applicable tax incentives, and is comfortable working with an international technology business.

Key Responsibilities

- Maintain local accounting records in accordance with Serbian accounting standards and regulations.

- Manage payroll calculations, employment-related taxes, social contributions, and employee reporting.

- Prepare and submit tax returns and ensure timely payment of tax liabilities.

- Assess applicable employment-related tax incentives and advise on compliant ways to optimize employment costs.

- Prepare and submit required reports to the National Bank of Serbia.

- Support international payments, prepare supporting documentation, and respond to inquiries from banks and relevant authorities.

- Prepare consolidated financial statements in accordance with IFRS.

- Monitor changes in Serbian accounting, tax, and employment regulations and implement relevant updates.

- Maintain accurate records and manage reporting deadlines independently.

Required Qualifications

- Based in Serbia, with practical experience independently managing accounting for a Serbian legal entity.

- Strong knowledge of Serbian accounting standards, tax legislation, statutory reporting requirements, and employment regulations relevant to payroll.

- Hands-on experience with payroll, employment-related taxes, and social contributions.

- Practical knowledge of employment-related tax incentives, including eligibility assessment and supporting documentation.

- Relevant professional accounting license or certification required for the scope of services.

- Experience preparing financial statements and consolidated reporting under IFRS.

- Experience with National Bank of Serbia reporting and international payments.

- Proficiency with Serbian reporting portals, accounting software, and Excel.

- Ability to communicate effectively in Serbian and English.

- Strong attention to detail, ownership, and the ability to meet deadlines independently.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience in an IT, SaaS, fintech, or gaming company.

- Experience working with international groups and intercompany transactions.

- Familiarity with modern accounting systems and automation tools.

Working Arrangement

- Part-time engagement with a regular workload of up to 20 hours per week.

- Freelance / independent contractor arrangement at this stage.

- Individual engagement with personal responsibility for day-to-day delivery.

Why Join Us

- World-class team – work alongside experienced professionals from around the globe who have built products used by millions of players

- High growth, high impact – be part of a fast-growing company where ideas turn into products and reach customers in days, not months

- Autonomy and ownership – we trust people to make decisions, take initiative, and drive results

- Modern tools and technology – use AI, automation, and modern tools as part of your everyday work

- Equity – participate in the company's growth and long-term success

posts.title: Solutions Engineer
posts.post:
The Role
This is a client-facing technical role at the intersection of customers, product, and applied AI. You'll work directly with American manufacturers to understand how their business operates, turn messy requirements into clear agent behaviors, and deploy a reliable Frank that delivers measurable value.
You'll own customer agent deployments end-to-end: map workflows, prioritize requirements, write SOPs and prompts, build evals, configure tools and guardrails, launch with users, and improve performance over time. The inputs are real and imperfect: dirty PDFs, legacy data, tribal knowledge, and edge cases that break naive systems.
The work is hands-on, fast-moving, and deeply user-centric. You'll work with LLMs and code every day, communicate directly with customer teams, and turn what you learn in the field into better product capabilities and a faster, more repeatable deployment system.
What you’ll do

- Lead agent deployments from discovery and requirements scoping through configuration, go-live, quantified ROI, and ongoing improvement

- Map complex customer workflows and turn them into focused requirements, SOPs, prompts, tools, guardrails, approvals, and handoffs

- Build evals and test cases that measure agent quality, expose failure modes, and guide iteration

- Configure and launch agents, monitor their real-world performance, investigate failures, and improve reliability over time

- Run customer workshops, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and close every dependency and follow-up needed to keep deployments moving

- Learn complex customer domains quickly and advocate for customer needs with product and engineering

- Turn repeated deployment problems into reusable patterns, tooling, and product improvements that make future launches faster

Who you are

- You have 4+ years of experience in software engineering or a client-facing technical role such as forward deployed engineering, solutions engineering, or implementation consulting

- You are technically strong and comfortable writing code, prompting LLMs, building evals, and learning new agent-engineering techniques

- You can scope ambiguous requirements, prioritize aggressively, and design a simple solution within real product and operational constraints

- You are an exceptional communicator who can run a customer workshop, present with confidence, and build trust from the shop floor to the executive team

- You are highly organized and process-oriented: you can manage multiple deployments, track details, use metrics, and close every loop

- You learn complex domains quickly and combine customer empathy with a product mindset, turning field insights into better tools and experiences

- You are ambitious, resourceful, action-oriented, and team-first; you care about strengthening American manufacturing and are excited to work in person five days a week in NYC and travel to customer sites across the US

Bonus points

- Experience building and operating agentic systems in production

- Experience in manufacturing or another industrial or operationally complex setting

- Experience creating SOPs or leading change-management work

- Experience integrating and deploying third-party APIs or legacy systems

About Forgepoint
Revitalize an industry. Rebuild America's manufacturing backbone.
America builds satellites, jet engines, and semiconductors with world-class precision, but the software running factory offices is decades behind. Estimators, procurement teams, and accountants still lose hours to spreadsheets, PDFs, and manual data entry.
Forgepoint builds AI workers for back office departments like quoting, purchasing, invoicing, and sales coordination. By removing back-office bottlenecks, we help US manufacturers move faster, grow, and compete globally.
We're backed by a16z speedrun and angels from Brex, Xwing, and Betterment. Join us in rebuilding the digital foundation of American manufacturing.
Our Founders
Jack Strauss — Co-Founder & CEO
Jack began his career at Acer and Northrop Grumman, then advised industrial companies at Bain. At Xwing, he helped scale the company and led GTM through its acquisition by Joby Aviation. He holds an MBA from Stanford and a BA from USC.
Alex Pareto — Co-Founder & CTO
Alex began his career at Meta, founded YC-backed Demeanor, and joined NTWRK after its acquisition. He later became a founding engineer on Brex Spend Management and led its engineering organization. He holds a BS in Computer Science from USC.
How we work

- In person every day in NYC for high-bandwidth collaboration

- Talk to users constantly: we build with manufacturers, not for them

- Own outcomes end-to-end and drive solutions without waiting for permission

Our Values

- We're Here to Win: We are building to help American manufacturers, our customers, our company, and our teammates win at the highest level.

- There's Always a Way: We are relentlessly resourceful, take ownership of constraints, and find a path forward when others stop.

- Truth Over Comfort: We choose honesty over ego, surface reality quickly, and change course when the facts demand it.

- Act Now: We move fast, trust our instincts, and correct course as we go.

- Step Up: We act like founders, fill gaps, fix problems, and follow through until the work is done.

- The Team. The Team. The Team.: We put the team first, push and support each other, share wins, and own failures together.

Comp & Benefits

- Base salary $175,000-$215,000 depending on level and experience, plus the opportunity to receive meaningful early-stage equity ($50,000-$90,000 per year) in Forgepoint. You'll also have great healthcare coverage, dinner provided at the office, and unlimited Celsius.

Location

- You'll be in our NYC office five days a week. If you're looking for a role where the real work happens somewhere else, this isn't it; if you want to be at the center of both the company and the customer, it is.

posts.title: Fabricator (Prototyping)
posts.post:
Runware develops AI infrastructure and modular data centres. We are hiring a hands-on Fabricator (Prototyping) to turn engineering designs into working prototype hardware using CNC machining, automated welding and precision assembly.
This role is for someone who enjoys owning the engineering: performing the calculations, making consequential design decisions, producing the documentation needed to build equipment, and proving its performance through testing.
About the role
You will be the person who makes our next generation designs real. Working closely with mechanical and systems engineers, you will machine, weld and assemble prototype components, then help refine them through fast build-test-iterate cycles.
The work spans one-off parts to small pilot runs. You will own fabrication quality from raw stock to finished assembly, and your feedback on manufacturability will shape the next design revision.
Key responsibilities

- Set up, program and operate CNC mills, lathes and other numerically controlled equipment from 2D drawings and 3D CAD models.

- Program, set up and run automated and robotic welding cells (MIG/TIG), including fixture design and parameter tuning.

- Assemble mechanical and electromechanical prototypes, sub-assemblies and test rigs to specification.

- Read and interpret engineering drawings, GD&T callouts, weld symbols and bills of materials.

- Inspect parts with calipers, micrometers, height gauges and other metrology tools; document results.

- Build jigs, fixtures and tooling that speed up repeat fabrication.

- Give engineers early feedback on manufacturability, tolerances, material choice and cost.

- Maintain machines and tools, and keep the workshop safe, clean and organised. Track material usage and help manage stock, consumables and supplier orders. Follow health, safety and environmental rules for machining, welding and pressure work.

Requirements

- Based in Bucharest or the Bucharest–Ilfov metropolitan area and able to work on-site.

- 3+ years of hands-on experience in fabrication, machining or a prototype workshop.

- Proven experience with numerical control (NC) based fabrication and CNC machining, including G-code and CAM programming (e.g. Fusion 360, Mastercam, SolidCAM).

- Experience setting up and running automated or robotic welding systems, plus solid manual MIG/TIG skills on steel, stainless steel and aluminium.

- Experience assembling prototypes from drawings, including mechanical fit-up, fastening and basic electrical wiring.

- Ability to read technical drawings, GD&T and weld symbols, and to work to tight tolerances.

- Confident use of precision measuring tools and basic quality documentation.

- Vocational or technical qualification in machining, welding or mechanical engineering, or equivalent experience.

- Fluent Romanian and English (technical documentation is in English).

Nice to have

- Experience fabricating components for high-pressure systems: piping, manifolds, vessels or fittings, including leak and pressure testing.

- Experience with refrigeration or HVAC-R components: copper and stainless tubing, brazing, flaring and swaging, heat exchangers.

- Familiarity with pressure equipment standards (e.g. PED 2014/68/EU, ASME) and ISCIR requirements in Romania.

- Welder certification to ISO 9606 or equivalent; refrigerant handling (F-gas) certification.

- CAD skills (SolidWorks, Fusion 360 or similar) to adjust parts and design fixtures.

- Experience with sheet metal (laser or waterjet cutting, press brake) or additive manufacturing.

- Experience in a startup or R&D environment with fast-changing priorities.

Benefits

- Competitive salary

- Real ownership: your builds go straight into prototypes and pilot hardware.

- A modern workshop and budget for the tools the job needs.

- Training and certification support (welding, pressure equipment, F-gas).

- A small, technical team where your input changes the design.

Applications without a portfolio will not be considered.
